html:
The first contest of tragedy at the City Dionysia, the spring festival of the god Dionysus in Athens, held around 534 BCE. Ancient tradition says it was won by Thespis.

Before this, choruses sang and danced hymns to Dionysus. Thespis is said to have stepped out of the chorus as a single actor who spoke lines and played a character, so that a story could be acted out. Actors are still called thespians after him.

The festival had been built up under the tyrant Pisistratus. Each year three playwrights each put on a set of plays, paid for by rich citizens, and judges chose a winner. Within two generations the form grew fast: Aeschylus added a second actor and Sophocles a third. The plays of Aeschylus, Sophocles and Euripides are the foundation of Western drama, and the Dionysia also gave rise to comedy.
